title.zh: 卷443 列傳二百三十 孙家鼐 张百熙 唐景崇 於式枚 沈家本
title.en: Volume 443 Biographies 230: Sun Jianai, Zhang Baixi, Tang Jingchong, Yu Shimei, Shen Jiaben
title.raw: 卷443 列傳二百三十 孙家鼐 张百熙 唐景崇 於式枚 沈家本

sentences.zh: 孫家鼐，字燮臣，安徽壽州人。

translations.literal: Sun Jianai, zi Xiechen, a man of Shouzhou, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jianai, whose courtesy name was Xiechen, was a native of Shouzhou in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 咸豐九年一甲一名進士，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xianfeng he was jinshi of the first rank in the first class; he was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Xianfeng reign he placed first among the first class of metropolitan graduates and was appointed Drafting Compiler.

sentences.zh: 歷侍讀，入直上書房。

translations.literal: He successively served as Reader-in-Waiting and entered regular attendance in the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the post of Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting and entered regular service in the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，命在毓慶宮行走，與尚書翁同龢授上讀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he was ordered to attend at the Yuying Palace, and together with Minister Weng Tonghe he instructed the emperor in reading.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Guangxu he was ordered to serve at the Yuying Palace, and together with Minister Weng Tonghe he taught the emperor his lessons.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士，擢工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was steadily promoted to Grand Secretariat Academician and elevated to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Grand Secretariat Academician and then elevated to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 江西學政陳寶琛疏請以先儒黃宗羲、顧炎武從祀文廟，議者多以爲未可，家鼐與潘祖蔭、翁同龢、孫詒經等再請，始議准。

translations.literal: The Jiangxi educational commissioner Chen Baochen memorialized requesting that the earlier Confucians Huang Zongxi and Gu Yanwu be admitted to sacrifices in the Confucian temple. Many in the discussion held this inadvisable. Jianai, together with Pan Zuyin, Weng Tonghe, Sun Yijing and others, petitioned again, and only then was it approved in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiangxi educational commissioner Chen Baochen memorialized that the earlier Confucians Huang Zongxi and Gu Yanwu be admitted to sacrifices in the Confucian temple, many officials argued against it. Jianai joined Pan Zuyin, Weng Tonghe, Sun Yijing, and others in petitioning again, and only then was the proposal approved.

sentences.zh: 十六年，授都察院左都御史、工部尚書，兼順天府尹。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left at the Censorate and Minister of Works, while also holding the post of Governor of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate and Minister of Works, while also serving as Governor of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二十年，中日事起，朝議主戰，家鼐力言釁不可啓。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, with the outbreak of affairs between China and Japan, court opinion favored war. Jianai strongly argued that hostilities must not be provoked.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, when war broke out between China and Japan, the court largely favored fighting. Jianai argued forcefully that hostilities must not be provoked.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，以吏部尚書協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, as Minister of Personnel he served as Assistant Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he served as Minister of Personnel and Assistant Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 命爲管學大臣。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as Superintendent of Studies.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Superintendent of Studies.

sentences.zh: 時方議變法，廢科舉，興學校，設報編書，皆特交核覆，家鼐一裁以正。

translations.literal: At that time reform was under discussion: abolishing the civil service examinations, establishing schools, founding newspapers, and compiling books—all were specially referred to him for review and reply; Jianai adjudicated each matter on proper grounds.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court was debating reform—abolishing the examinations, founding schools, establishing newspapers, and commissioning books—and each proposal was referred to him for review. Jianai judged every matter on its merits.

sentences.zh: 嘗疏謂：「國家廣集卿士以資議政，聽言固不厭求詳，然執兩用中，精擇審處，尤賴聖知。」

translations.literal: He once memorialized, saying: "The state broadly gathers ministers and scholars to supply material for policy deliberation. In listening to words, one certainly does not tire of seeking detail; yet to hold to the mean between two extremes and carefully choose and settle matters especially relies on sagely discernment."
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized: "The state gathers ministers and scholars broadly so that they may inform deliberation on policy. In hearing counsel one should never weary of seeking thoroughness, yet to hold the mean between opposing views and to choose and settle matters with care depends above all on the sovereign's discernment."

sentences.zh: 其所建議，類能持大體。

translations.literal: His recommendations for the most part were able to uphold the larger principles.
translations.idiomatic: For the most part his recommendations upheld the larger principles of governance.

sentences.zh: 及議廢立，家鼐獨持不可。

translations.literal: When the question of deposing and enthroning came under discussion, Jianai alone maintained that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated deposing and enthroning the emperor, Jianai alone held that it must not be done.

sentences.zh: 旋以病乞罷。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he begged to retire on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he asked to resign on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，乘輿西狩，召赴行在，起禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when the imperial carriage went west on campaign, he was summoned to the traveling court and reappointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, when the court fled west, he was summoned to the traveling palace and reappointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 還京，拜體仁閣大學士。

translations.literal: After returning to the capital he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tiren Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the capital he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tiren Hall.

sentences.zh: 歷轉東閣、文淵閣，晉武英殿。

translations.literal: He successively transferred to the Dongge and Wenyuange halls, and was promoted to the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn at the Dongge and Wenyuange halls and was promoted to the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 充學務大臣，裁度規章，折衷中外，嚴定宗旨，一以敦行實學爲主，學風爲之一靖。

translations.literal: As Superintendent of Educational Affairs he framed regulations, balancing Chinese and foreign models, strictly fixing the guiding purpose so that practical learning in earnest conduct was paramount; scholarly manners were thereby calmed.
translations.idiomatic: As Superintendent of Educational Affairs he drafted regulations, balancing Chinese and Western models and fixing a clear purpose with practical learning at its core. Scholarly conduct was thereby steadied.

sentences.zh: 議改官制，命與慶親王奕劻、軍機大臣瞿鴻禨總司核定。

translations.literal: When reform of the official system was discussed, he was ordered together with Prince Qing Yikuang and Grand Councilor Qu Hongji to take chief charge of verification and approval.
translations.idiomatic: When reform of the official system was discussed, he was ordered to work with Prince Qing Yikuang and Grand Councilor Qu Hongji as chief coordinators of the review.

sentences.zh: 御史趙啓霖劾奕劻及其子貝子載振受賄納優，命醇親王載灃與家鼐往按，啓霖坐汚衊親貴褫職，而載振尋亦乞罷兼官。

translations.literal: Censor Zhao Qilin impeached Yikuang and his son the beizi Zaizhen for accepting bribes and taking in actresses. The order went out for Prince Chun Zaifeng and Jianai to go investigate. Zhao Qilin was punished for defaming imperial kin and stripped of office, while Zaizhen soon also begged to resign his concurrent posts.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhao Qilin impeached Yikuang and his son, the beizi Zaizhen, for taking bribes and keeping actresses. Prince Chun Zaifeng and Jianai were sent to investigate. Zhao Qilin was punished for slandering imperial kin and stripped of office, and Zaizhen soon resigned his concurrent posts as well.

sentences.zh: 資政院立，命貝子溥倫及家鼐爲總裁，一持正議不阿。

translations.literal: When the Political Consultative Assembly was established, the order appointed Beizi Pulun and Jianai as presidents. Jianai consistently held to upright views and did not flatter.
translations.idiomatic: When the Political Consultative Assembly was established, the beizi Pulun and Jianai were appointed its presidents. Jianai consistently upheld principled views and would not curry favor.

sentences.zh: 時詔諸臣輪班進講，家鼐撰尚書四子書講義以進。

translations.literal: At that time an edict directed all ministers to take turns lecturing before the throne. Jianai composed lectures on the Book of Documents and the Four Books and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time an edict required ministers to lecture before the throne in rotation. Jianai composed and presented lectures on the Book of Documents and the Four Books.

sentences.zh: 三十四年二月，以鄉舉重逢，賞太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirty-fourth year, because he had again encountered the provincial examination cycle of his own success, he was rewarded with the rank of Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the thirty-fourth year, because he had again reached the anniversary of his provincial examination success, he was granted the title Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 歷蒙賜「壽」，頒賞御書及諸珍品，賜紫韁，紫禁城內坐二人暖輪，恩遇優渥。

translations.literal: He repeatedly received gifts of the character "Longevity," imperial calligraphy and various precious objects, purple reins, and a two-seater heated carriage within the Forbidden City. His gracious treatment was exceptionally generous.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly received the gift of the character "Longevity," imperial calligraphy, and other precious objects, along with purple reins and a heated two-seat carriage within the Forbidden City. The favor shown him was exceptionally generous.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，再疏乞病，溫詔慰留。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong he again memorialized begging leave on grounds of illness, and a warm edict urged him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuantong he again asked to retire on grounds of illness, and a gracious edict urged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年八十有二，贈太傅，諡文正。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died, aged eighty-two. He was posthumously granted Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Wen Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward, at the age of eighty-two. He was posthumously granted the title Grand Tutor and given the posthumous name Wen Zheng.

sentences.zh: 家鼐簡約斂退，生平無疾言遽色。

translations.literal: Jianai was simple and restrained in manner, retiring in deportment. Throughout his life he never spoke harshly or showed sudden anger.
translations.idiomatic: Jianai lived simply and modestly. Throughout his life he never spoke harshly or showed sudden anger.

sentences.zh: 雖貴，與諸生鈞禮。

translations.literal: Though honored in rank, he treated scholars with equality in ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Though he rose to high rank, he treated scholars as equals.

sentences.zh: 閉門齋居，雜賓遠跡，推避權勢若怯。

translations.literal: He lived behind closed doors in purification, keeping casual guests at a distance, and shrank from powerful connections as if from fear.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his doors closed and lived in quiet seclusion, keeping casual visitors at a distance and shunning powerful connections as if from timidity.

sentences.zh: 嘗督湖北學政，典山西試，再典順天試，總裁會試，屢充閱卷大臣，獨無所私。

translations.literal: He once supervised educational affairs in Hubei, presided over the Shanxi examination, twice presided over the Shuntian examination, served as chief examiner of the metropolitan examination, and repeatedly served as chief reviewing examiner—all without favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: He once supervised education in Hubei, presided over the Shanxi provincial examination, twice presided over the Shuntian examination, served as chief examiner of the metropolitan examination, and repeatedly served as chief reviewing examiner—never showing favoritism.

sentences.zh: 嘗拔一卷廁二甲，同列意不可，即屏退之，其讓不喜競類此。

translations.literal: He once pulled up one examination paper to the second rank of the second class. His colleagues disapproved and he immediately set it aside and rejected it. His yielding and dislike of competition were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Once he placed a candidate's paper in the second rank of the second class, but when his colleagues objected he immediately set it aside. His willingness to yield and his dislike of rivalry were characteristic.

sentences.zh: 器量尤廣，庚子，外人請懲禍首戮大臣，編修劉廷琛謂失國體，責宰輔不能爭，家鼐揖而引過。

translations.literal: His breadth of mind was especially great. In the gengzi year foreigners demanded punishment of those responsible and execution of great ministers. Compiler Liu Tingchen said this would lose national dignity and blamed the chief ministers for failing to protest. Jianai bowed and took the blame upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: His breadth of character was especially remarkable. In the gengzi year foreigners demanded that those responsible be punished and senior ministers executed. Compiler Liu Tingchen said this would disgrace the state and blamed the chief ministers for failing to object. Jianai bowed and took the blame upon himself.

sentences.zh: 其後詔舉御史。

translations.literal: Afterward an edict called for recommendations of censors.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict called for nominations of censors.

sentences.zh: 家鼐獨保廷琛，謂曩以大義見責，知忠鯁必不負國，世皆稱之。

translations.literal: Jianai alone recommended Tingchen, saying that because he had once been rebuked on grounds of great principle, one knew that as a loyal and forthright man he would not fail the state. The world praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Jianai alone recommended Tingchen, saying that because he had once been rebuked for upholding a great principle, one could know that as a loyal and forthright man he would not fail the state. The world praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 張百熙，字埜秋，長沙人。

translations.literal: Zhang Baixi, zi Yeqiu, a man of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Baixi, whose courtesy name was Yeqiu, was a native of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 同治十三年進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tongzhi he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Tongzhi he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 督山東學政，典試四川。

translations.literal: He supervised educational affairs in Shandong and presided over the examination in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised education in Shandong and presided over the provincial examination in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 命直南書房，再遷侍讀。

translations.literal: He was ordered to regular attendance in the Southern Imperial Library and was twice promoted to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to regular service in the Southern Imperial Library and was promoted twice to Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十年，朝鮮釁起，朝議多主戰。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Guangxu trouble broke out in Korea. Court opinion largely favored war.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Guangxu conflict broke out in Korea, and most at court favored war.

sentences.zh: 百熙疏劾李鴻章陽作戰備，陰實主和，左寶貴、聶士成皆勇敢善戰之將，以餉械不繼，遂致敗績，咎在鴻章；

translations.literal: Baixi memorialized impeaching Li Hongzhang for openly making war preparations while in fact favoring peace. Zuo Baogui and Nie Shicheng were both brave generals skilled in battle, but because funds and weapons were not supplied in sequence they therefore suffered defeat—the fault lay with Hongzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Baixi memorialized against Li Hongzhang, charging that he made a show of preparing for war while secretly favoring peace. Zuo Baogui and Nie Shicheng were both brave and capable generals, but because pay and arms were not supplied in time they were defeated—the blame lay with Hongzhang.

sentences.zh: 又劾禮親王世鐸筦樞務，招權納賄，戰事起，一倚鴻章，貽誤兵機：皆不報。

translations.literal: He also impeached Prince Su Shiduo for managing Grand Council affairs, monopolizing power and taking bribes. When war began he relied entirely on Hongzhang and thereby botched military timing. All these memorials went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Prince Li Shiduo for monopolizing Grand Council affairs, hoarding power, and taking bribes; when war began Shiduo relied entirely on Hongzhang and thereby mishandled military timing. None of these memorials received a response.

sentences.zh: 時值太后萬壽，承辦典禮者猶競尚華飾，百熙奏罷之。

translations.literal: At that time it was the empress dowager's birthday celebration. Those in charge of the ceremonies still vied in extravagant display. Baixi memorialized to stop this.
translations.idiomatic: It was the empress dowager's birthday, yet those in charge of the ceremonies still competed in lavish display. Baixi memorialized to put a stop to it.

sentences.zh: 復偕侍講學士陸寶忠等合彈樞臣朋比誤國十大罪。

translations.literal: He again joined Lecturer Lu Baozhong and others in jointly impeaching the Grand Council ministers on ten capital crimes of faction and harming the state.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Lecturer Lu Baozhong and others in jointly impeaching the Grand Council ministers on ten capital charges of factional collusion and harming the state.

sentences.zh: 未幾，孫毓汶引疾歸，恭親王奕訢復入軍機，而百熙亦出督廣東學政。

translations.literal: Before long Sun Yuwen retired on grounds of illness and returned home. Prince Gong Yixin reentered the Grand Council, and Baixi also went out to supervise educational affairs in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Sun Yuwen retired on grounds of illness, Prince Gong Yixin returned to the Grand Council, and Baixi was sent out to supervise education in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was steadily promoted to Grand Secretariat Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Grand Secretariat Academician.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，坐濫舉康有爲，革職留任。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, for indiscriminate recommendation of Kang Youwei, he was stripped of office but kept in his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was punished for indiscriminately recommending Kang Youwei: his office was stripped but he was kept in post.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授禮部侍郎，擢左都御史，充頭等專使大臣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Left, and appointed Chief Envoy of the First Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief, and made a chief envoy of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 拳匪亂定，下詔求言，百熙抗疏陳大計，請改官制，理財政，變科舉，建學堂，設報館。

translations.literal: After the Boxer disturbance was settled, an edict was issued seeking opinions. Baixi submitted a forthright memorial stating the great plan, requesting reform of the official system, regulation of finances, transformation of the examination system, establishment of schools, and founding of newspapers.
translations.idiomatic: After the Boxer uprising was suppressed, the throne issued an edict seeking counsel. Baixi submitted a forthright memorial outlining a grand plan: reform the official system, put finances in order, transform the examinations, establish schools, and found newspapers.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷工部尚書，調刑部，充管學大臣。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Minister of Works, then to the Ministry of Punishments, and appointed Superintendent of Studies.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Minister of Works, transferred to the Ministry of Punishments, and appointed Superintendent of Studies.

sentences.zh: 京師之有大學堂也，始於中日戰後。

translations.literal: The Imperial University in the capital had its beginning after the Sino-Japanese War.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial University in the capital dated from the period after the Sino-Japanese War.

sentences.zh: 侍郎李端棻奏請立學，中旨報可，而樞府厭言新政，請緩行。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Li Duanfen memorialized requesting establishment of a school. The imperial rescript approved, but the Grand Council was weary of speaking of new policies and requested postponement.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Li Duanfen memorialized asking that a university be established. The imperial rescript approved, but the Grand Council was weary of new policies and asked that implementation be delayed.

sentences.zh: 迄戊戌，乃奉嚴旨，促擬學章，命孫家鼐爲管學大臣。

translations.literal: By the wuxu year a stern edict finally came, pressing for draft school regulations, and Sun Jianai was ordered as Superintendent of Studies.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the wuxu year did a stern edict come pressing for draft school regulations, and Sun Jianai was appointed Superintendent of Studies.

sentences.zh: 及政變，惟大學以萌芽早得不廢。

translations.literal: When the political coup came, only the university, because it had sprouted early, escaped abolition.
translations.idiomatic: When the political coup came, only the university survived abolition, because it had taken root early.

sentences.zh: 許景澄繼管學，坐論義和團被誅。

translations.literal: Xu Jingcheng succeeded as superintendent of studies and was executed for speaking against the Boxers.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingcheng succeeded him as superintendent of studies and was executed for criticizing the Boxers.

sentences.zh: 兩宮西幸，百熙詣行在，以人望被斯任，於是海內欣然望興學矣。

translations.literal: When the two palaces went west, Baixi went to the traveling court. Because of his public stature he received this appointment, and throughout the realm people gladly looked to the revival of learning.
translations.idiomatic: When the two palaces fled west, Baixi went to the traveling court. Because of his public standing he received the appointment, and throughout the empire people looked eagerly to the revival of learning.

sentences.zh: 百熙奏加冀州知州吳汝綸五品卿銜，總教大學。

translations.literal: Baixi memorialized adding the Prefect of Jizhou Wu Jilun to fifth-rank minister status and making him general instructor of the university.
translations.idiomatic: Baixi memorialized that Wu Rulun, prefect of Jizhou, be given fifth-rank minister status and made general instructor of the university.

sentences.zh: 汝綸辭不應，百熙具衣冠拜之，汝綸請赴日本察視學務。

translations.literal: Jilun declined and would not accept. Baixi, fully robed, bowed to him. Jilun requested to go to Japan to observe educational affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jilun declined. Baixi, fully robed, bowed to him in person. Jilun then asked to go to Japan to observe educational affairs.

sentences.zh: 大學教職員皆自聘，又薪金優厚，忌嫉者衆，蜚語浸聞。

translations.literal: All the university's teaching staff were hired on his own initiative, and salaries were generous. Those who envied him were many, and slander gradually reached the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He hired all the university's teaching staff himself and paid generous salaries. Many envied him, and slander gradually reached the court.

sentences.zh: 汝綸返國，未至京，卒；

translations.literal: Jilun returned to the country but died before reaching the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jilun returned to China but died before he reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 而百熙所倚以辦學者，門人沈兆祉亦受讒搆。

translations.literal: And Shen Zhaozhi, a disciple on whom Baixi relied to manage the school, also fell victim to slander and framing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhaozhi, a disciple on whom Baixi relied to run the school, also fell victim to slander and intrigue.

sentences.zh: 大學既負時謗，言官奏稱本朝定制，部官大率滿、漢相維，請更設滿大臣主教事，乃增命榮慶爲管學大臣。

translations.literal: The university already bore contemporary blame. Censorial officials memorialized saying that according to this dynasty's established system, ministry officials are largely interwoven Manchu and Han. They requested additionally appointing a Manchu grand minister to preside, and Rongqing was added as Superintendent of Studies.
translations.idiomatic: The university was already widely criticized. Censorial officials memorialized that under dynastic custom ministry offices were generally shared between Manchu and Han officials, and asked that a Manchu grand minister be added to preside. Rongqing was accordingly appointed co-superintendent of studies.

sentences.zh: 旋別設學務處，以張亨嘉爲大學總監督，百熙權益分。

translations.literal: Soon a separate Board of Educational Affairs was established, with Zhang Hengjia as general superintendent of the university. Baixi's authority was correspondingly divided.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a separate Board of Educational Affairs was established, with Zhang Hengjia as general superintendent of the university, and Baixi's authority was correspondingly divided.

sentences.zh: 始議分建七科大學，又選派諸生游學東西洋。

translations.literal: At first they discussed establishing seven specialized universities and also selecting students to study in East Asia and the West.
translations.idiomatic: At first they discussed establishing seven specialized universities and selecting students to study in East Asia and the West.

sentences.zh: 榮慶意不謂可，而百熙持之堅，親至站送諸生登車。

translations.literal: Rongqing did not consider this advisable, but Baixi held firm. In person he went to the station to see the students off as they boarded the train.
translations.idiomatic: Rongqing did not think it advisable, but Baixi held firm and went in person to the station to see the students off as they boarded the train.

sentences.zh: 各省之派官費生自此始。

translations.literal: Provincial governments dispatching students at government expense began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial governments sending students abroad at government expense began from this.

sentences.zh: 值張之洞入覲，命改定學章，及還鎮，復命家鼐爲管學大臣。

translations.literal: When Zhang Zhidong came to court for audience, he was ordered to revise the school regulations. When he returned to his post, Sun Jianai was again ordered as Superintendent of Studies.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhidong came to court for audience he was ordered to revise the school regulations. When he returned to his post, Sun Jianai was again appointed Superintendent of Studies.

sentences.zh: 凡三管學，百熙位第三矣。

translations.literal: In all there were three superintendents of studies; Baixi stood third.
translations.idiomatic: There were three superintendents of studies in all; Baixi was the third.

sentences.zh: 百熙擬建分科大學，以絀於貲而止，惟創醫學及譯學館、實業館，遽謝學務。

translations.literal: Baixi planned to build specialized universities but stopped for lack of funds. Only the medical college and schools of translation and practical industry were created, and he quickly resigned from educational affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Baixi planned to build specialized universities but stopped for lack of funds. He created only a medical college and schools of translation and practical industry, then quickly resigned from educational affairs.

sentences.zh: 賞黃馬褂、紫禁城騎馬。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with the yellow jacket and permission to ride a horse within the Forbidden City.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the yellow jacket and permission to ride a horse within the Forbidden City.

sentences.zh: 後歷禮部、戶部、郵傳部尚書，政務、學務、編纂官制諸大臣。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as Minister of Rites, Revenue, and Posts and Communications, and as minister of government affairs, educational affairs, and compilation of the official system reform.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served in succession as Minister of Rites, Revenue, and Posts and Communications, and as minister of government affairs, educational affairs, and compilation of the official system reform.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少保，諡文達。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince with posthumous title Wen Da.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince with the posthumous name Wen Da.

sentences.zh: 唐景崇，字春卿，廣西灌陽人。

translations.literal: Tang Jingchong, zi Chunqing, a man of Guanyang, Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jingchong, whose courtesy name was Chunqing, was a native of Guanyang in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 父懋功，舉人，有學行。

translations.literal: His father Maogong was a provincial graduate with learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His father Maogong was a provincial graduate known for learning and integrity.

sentences.zh: 景崇，同治十年進士，授編修。

translations.literal: Jingchong passed the metropolitan examination in the tenth year of Tongzhi and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong passed the metropolitan examination in the tenth year of Tongzhi and was appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 由侍讀四遷至內閣學士。

translations.literal: From Reader-in-Waiting he was promoted four times to Grand Secretariat Academician.
translations.idiomatic: From Reader-in-Waiting he was promoted four times to Grand Secretariat Academician.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十年，典試廣東。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Guangxu he presided over the Guangdong examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Guangxu he presided over the Guangdong provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 明年，主會試。

translations.literal: The next year he served as chief examiner of the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he served as chief examiner of the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 歷兵部、禮部侍郎，權左都御史，出督浙江學政，母憂歸。

translations.literal: He successively served as Vice Minister of War and Rites, acted as Censor-in-Chief of the Left, went out to supervise educational affairs in Zhejiang, and returned home on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Vice Minister of War and Rites, acted as Left Censor-in-Chief, went out to supervise education in Zhejiang, and returned home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 拳禍起，命督辦廣西團練。

translations.literal: When the Boxer calamity arose he was ordered to supervise organization of Guangxi militia training.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer uprising broke out he was ordered to supervise militia training in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以工部侍郎典試浙江，督江蘇學政，三十一年，詔罷科歲試，學政專司考校學務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, as Vice Minister of Works he presided over the Zhejiang examination and supervised educational affairs in Jiangsu. In the thirty-first year an edict abolished the annual provincial examinations and restricted educational commissioners to examining and supervising academic affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, as Vice Minister of Works, he presided over the Zhejiang examination and supervised education in Jiangsu. In the thirty-first year an edict abolished the annual provincial examinations and confined educational commissioners to examining and supervising academic affairs.

sentences.zh: 景崇條上十事。

translations.literal: Jingchong listed ten items in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong memorialized ten proposals in detail.

sentences.zh: 明年，罷學政，還京供職。

translations.literal: The next year the post of educational commissioner was abolished. He returned to the capital to serve.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the post of educational commissioner was abolished, and he returned to the capital to resume office.

sentences.zh: 疏陳立憲大要四事。

translations.literal: He memorialized setting forth four main points regarding constitutional government.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized four main points on constitutional government.

sentences.zh: 時兩廣疆臣建議廣西省會移治南寧，京朝官皆持異議。

translations.literal: At that time the governors-general of the two Guang provinces proposed moving the provincial capital of Guangxi from Guilin to Nanning. Officials at the capital all held differing opinions.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the governors-general of the two Guang provinces proposed moving the Guangxi provincial capital from Guilin to Nanning. Officials at court were divided.

sentences.zh: 景崇奏陳：「遷省之議，以越南逼近龍州，法人時蓄狡謀，桂林距離遠，聲氣難通，不若改建南寧之便。

translations.literal: Jingchong memorialized, saying: "As for the proposal to move the provincial seat: because Vietnam presses close upon Longzhou and the French at times harbor crafty designs, and Guilin is far away so that voice and influence are hard to convey, it would be more convenient to rebuild at Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong memorialized: "Those who favor moving the provincial seat argue that Vietnam presses close on Longzhou, that the French often harbor crafty designs, and that Guilin is too distant for timely communication—so rebuilding at Nanning would be more convenient.

sentences.zh: 臣謂不然，今我兵力尚不能經營邕州，扼北海水陸衝要，徒虛張聲勢，招外人疑忌何爲？

translations.literal: I say this is not so. Today our military strength still cannot manage Yongzhou or hold the land and sea strategic points of Beihai. Merely to make a show of strength in empty fashion—what is the use of provoking foreigners' suspicion and jealousy?
translations.idiomatic: I disagree. Our forces are not yet strong enough to hold Yongzhou or control Beihai's land and sea approaches. To make an empty show of strength would only invite foreign suspicion—what good would that do?

sentences.zh: 且遷徙締造之費，桂林善後之費，練兵設防之費，皆非巨款不辦。

translations.literal: Moreover, the costs of migration and construction, the costs of dealing with Guilin afterward, and the costs of training troops and establishing defenses—all cannot be undertaken without huge funds.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the costs of relocation and construction, of dealing with Guilin afterward, and of training troops and building defenses cannot be met without enormous sums.

sentences.zh: 方今俄居西陲，英窺南徼，蒙、藏、川、滇勢均岌岌，非獨一法人之可畏。

translations.literal: At present Russia occupies the western frontier, England peers at the southern marches, and Mongolia, Tibet, Sichuan and Yunnan are all in equally precarious positions. It is not only the French who are to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Russia now holds the western frontier, Britain watches the southern marches, and Mongolia, Tibet, Sichuan, and Yunnan are all in peril. We have more to fear than France alone.

sentences.zh: 以大局論，決不能竭全力事廣西之一隅；

translations.literal: Speaking from the perspective of the overall situation, one certainly cannot exhaust all strength on one corner of Guangxi alone.
translations.idiomatic: From the perspective of the empire as a whole, we certainly cannot exhaust our strength on one corner of Guangxi alone.

sentences.zh: 以廣西論，亦不能竭全力事南寧之一隅：明矣。

translations.literal: Speaking from the perspective of Guangxi alone, one also certainly cannot exhaust all strength on the corner of Nanning alone—this is clear.
translations.idiomatic: And from Guangxi's perspective alone, we cannot exhaust our strength on Nanning alone either. That much is clear.

sentences.zh: 故爲今之計，誠能簡重臣駐龍州，於對汛邊地二千里，相度土宜，興辦樹藝、屯墾、畜牧、開礦諸端，俟地利漸興，人齒漸繁，再以兵法部勒。

translations.literal: Therefore for the present plan, if one can truly send a high minister of reduced rank to station at Longzhou, and over two thousand li of borderland facing the enemy outpost assess local suitability and undertake forestry, colonization, animal husbandry and mining, then when geographical advantage gradually flourishes and population gradually multiplies, one may afterward deploy them by military organization.
translations.idiomatic: The better course for the present would be to send a senior minister to Longzhou. Over two thousand li of borderland facing the enemy, assess local conditions and develop forestry, colonization, animal husbandry, and mining. When the land grows productive and population increases, troops can then be organized by military methods.

sentences.zh: 此上策也。

translations.literal: This is the superior policy.
translations.idiomatic: That is the superior strategy.

sentences.zh: 至目前應變之方，莫如迅設龍州電綫，移提督駐南寧，增募十營，暫停廣西應解賠款，飭各省欠解廣西協餉，分年攤解，用抵賠款。

translations.literal: As for present measures to meet change, none surpass swiftly establishing a telegraph line at Longzhou, moving the provincial military governor to Nanning, recruiting ten additional camps, temporarily suspending indemnity payments Guangxi should remit, and ordering provinces that owe Guangxi cooperative stipends to pay in installments year by year to offset indemnities.
translations.idiomatic: For immediate measures, nothing would be better than quickly establishing a telegraph line at Longzhou, moving the provincial military governor to Nanning, recruiting ten additional battalions, temporarily suspending Guangxi's indemnity payments, and ordering provinces that owe Guangxi cooperative stipends to pay in annual installments to offset those payments.

sentences.zh: 一轉移間，餉足則兵强，可紓朝廷南顧之憂。

translations.literal: In one turn of shifting, when stipends suffice the troops are strong and the court's anxiety over the south may be eased.
translations.idiomatic: With these shifts, once pay is sufficient the troops will be strong, and the court's anxiety over the south may be eased.

sentences.zh: 若遷省之舉，勞民費財，無益於治。」

translations.literal: As for the move of the provincial seat, it labors the people and wastes wealth without benefit to governance."
translations.idiomatic: As for moving the provincial seat, it would burden the people, waste resources, and do nothing for good governance."

sentences.zh: 事得寢。

translations.literal: The matter thereby came to rest.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 調吏部侍郎，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel and appointed lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel and appointed lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 景崇以績學端品受主知，屢司文柄。

translations.literal: Jingchong, because of solid learning and upright character, won the ruler's trust and repeatedly controlled literary examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his solid scholarship and upright character, Jingchong won the ruler's trust and repeatedly held control of literary examinations.

sentences.zh: 迨科舉罷，廷試游學畢業生，皆倚景崇校閱。

translations.literal: When the civil service examinations were abolished and palace examinations were held for graduates who had studied abroad, all relied on Jingchong for examination and review.
translations.idiomatic: When the civil service examinations were abolished and palace examinations were held for students who had studied abroad, all relied on Jingchong to examine and review them.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，戴鴻慈卒，遺疏薦景崇堪大用。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong, Dai Hongci died; in his final memorial he recommended Jingchong as fit for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xuantong reign Dai Hongci died; in his deathbed memorial he recommended Tang Jingchong as capable of great service.

sentences.zh: 二年，擢學部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year he was elevated to Minister of the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔設內閣，改學務大臣。

translations.literal: The next year an edict established the Grand Council; he was changed to Minister of Educational Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year an edict established the cabinet, and he was reassigned as Minister of Educational Affairs.

sentences.zh: 是時學說紛歧，景崇力謀溝通新舊，慎擇教科書。

translations.literal: At that time doctrines diverged; Jingchong strove to bridge old and new and carefully selected textbooks.
translations.idiomatic: At that time scholarly doctrines were sharply divided; Jingchong worked hard to reconcile the old and the new and to choose textbooks with care.

sentences.zh: 兼任弼德院顧問大臣。

translations.literal: He also served concurrently as Adviser Minister at the Bide Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He also served concurrently as an advising minister at the Bide Academy.

sentences.zh: 武昌變起，袁世凱總理內閣，仍命掌學務。

translations.literal: When the Wuchang revolt broke out, Yuan Shikai became Premier of the Grand Council; he was still ordered to direct educational affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuchang uprising broke out, Yuan Shikai became premier of the cabinet, yet Jingchong was still ordered to oversee educational affairs.

sentences.zh: 引疾去。

translations.literal: He cited illness and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 越三年，卒，諡文簡。

translations.literal: Three years later he died; posthumous title Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he died and was given the posthumous title Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 景崇博覽羣書，通天文算術，尤喜治史。

translations.literal: Jingchong read widely among books, mastered astronomy and calculation, and especially delighted in historical study.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong read widely, mastered astronomy and mathematics, and especially loved the study of history.

sentences.zh: 自爲編修時，取新唐書爲作注，大例有三：曰糾繆，曰補闕，曰疏解，甄采書逾數百種。

translations.literal: From his time as Compiler he annotated the New Book of Tang; the grand scheme had three parts—called correcting errors, filling lacunae, and explicating the text—and books examined and gathered exceeded several hundred kinds.
translations.idiomatic: From his days as a drafting compiler he undertook a commentary on the New Book of Tang organized under three headings: correcting errors, filling gaps, and clarifying the text, drawing on more than several hundred works.

sentences.zh: 家故貧，得秘籍精本，輒典質購之。

translations.literal: His family was originally poor; whenever he obtained rare books or fine editions he would pawn or mortgage to purchase them.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been poor; whenever he found a rare or fine edition he would pawn his belongings to buy it.

sentences.zh: 殫精畢世，唯缺地理志內羈縻州及藝文志，餘均脫稿。

translations.literal: He exhausted his spirit unto the end of his life; only the Geography Monograph's dependent states and the Bibliographic Monograph were lacking—all else had left draft.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted his utmost until the end of his life; only the sections on dependent prefectures in the Geography Monograph and the Bibliographic Monograph remained unfinished—everything else was in final draft.

sentences.zh: 于式枚，字晦若，賀縣人。

translations.literal: Yu Shimei, zi Huiruo, a man of He County.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shimei, whose courtesy name was Huiruo, was a native of He County.

sentences.zh: 博聞强記，善屬文。

translations.literal: Broad learning and powerful memory; skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed encyclopedic learning and a formidable memory, and was skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年進士，以庶吉士，散館用兵部主事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu he became jinshi; as a Bachelor he left the Hanlin Academy and was assigned as a Secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Guangxu reign he passed the metropolitan examination; after leaving the Hanlin Academy as a Bachelor he was assigned as a secretary in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章疏調北洋差遣，歷十餘年，奏牘多出其手。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang memorialized to transfer him for service in the Beiyang command; for more than ten years most memorials and documents issued from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang memorialized to have him transferred for service in the Beiyang command; for more than ten years most of the memorials and documents there came from his hand.

sentences.zh: 性不樂爲外吏，又格於例不得保升京秩，久之不遷。

translations.literal: By nature he did not enjoy serving as an outside official; moreover, blocked by regulations he could not obtain promotion to Beijing rank—long without advancement.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he disliked serving as a provincial official, and regulations also barred him from securing promotion to a capital post, so for a long time he received no advancement.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，鴻章賀俄皇加冕，因歷聘德、法、英、美諸國，式枚充隨員。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Hongzhang attended the Russian emperor's coronation; he then made successive embassies to Germany, France, Britain, America, and other states—Shimei served as attendant staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Li Hongzhang attended the coronation of the Russian emperor and then paid successive visits to Germany, France, Britain, the United States, and other countries, with Shimei serving on his staff.

sentences.zh: 俄選授禮部主事，由員外郎授御史，遷給事中。

translations.literal: Soon he was selected and appointed a Secretary in the Ministry of Rites; from Department Director he was appointed censor, then promoted to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon selected and appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Rites, then promoted from department director to censor and then to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 贊辛丑和約，賞五品京堂。

translations.literal: He assisted the Boxer Protocol; rewarded with fifth-rank Beijing office.
translations.idiomatic: He assisted in negotiating the Boxer Protocol and was rewarded with a fifth-rank capital office.

sentences.zh: 充政務處幫提調、大學堂總辦、譯學館監督。

translations.literal: He served as Assistant Coordinator at the Office of Government Affairs, Superintendent of the Imperial University, and Supervisor of the School of Translation.
translations.idiomatic: He served as assistant coordinator at the Office of Government Affairs, superintendent of the Imperial University, and supervisor of the School of Translation.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，以鴻臚寺少卿督廣東學政，改提學使，疏辭，命總理廣西鐵路。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments he supervised Guangdong educational affairs; changed to educational commissioner, memorialized refusal—ordered to direct Guangxi railways.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year, as vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments he was appointed to supervise educational affairs in Guangdong; when the post was changed to educational commissioner he memorialized to decline and was instead ordered to direct Guangxi railways.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，擢郵傳部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year promoted to Vice Minister of Posts and Communications.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he was promoted to vice minister of posts and communications.

sentences.zh: 當是時，政潮激烈，有詔預備立憲，舉朝競言西法，無敢持異議者。

translations.literal: At that time political currents were fierce; an edict prepared constitutionalism and the whole court vied to speak of Western methods—none dared hold differing views.
translations.idiomatic: At that time political currents ran fierce; an edict announced preparations for constitutional government, and the whole court competed to advocate Western methods, with no one daring to dissent.

sentences.zh: 於是式枚奉命出使德國，充考察憲政大臣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shimei received orders to go abroad to Germany as commissioner investigating constitutional government.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei was then ordered to go to Germany as commissioner to investigate constitutional government.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，疏言：「憲政必以本國爲根據，采取他國以輔益之，在求其實，不徒震其名。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure he memorialized, saying: "Constitutional government must take one's own country as foundation, adopt other countries to supplement and benefit—it lies in seeking what is real, not merely being awed by names.
translations.idiomatic: Before his departure he memorialized, saying: "Constitutional government must take one's own country as its foundation and adopt other countries only to supplement it; the aim is to seek what is real, not merely to be dazzled by names.

sentences.zh: 我朝道監百王，科條詳備，行政皆守部章，風聞亦許言事，刑賞予奪，曾不自私。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's Way oversees the hundred kings; regulations and items are detailed and complete; administration all follows ministry statutes; hearsay is also permitted to speak on affairs; punishments, rewards, grants and withholdings have never been selfish.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's Way has overseen the hundred kings; its regulations are detailed and complete, administration follows the statutes of each ministry, and even hearsay is permitted as grounds for memorializing; rewards and punishments have never been selfishly applied.

sentences.zh: 有大政事、大興革，內則集廷臣之議，外或待疆吏之章。

translations.literal: When there are great government affairs or great reforms and innovations, internally the court assembles ministers' deliberations; externally sometimes waits for frontier officials' memorials.
translations.idiomatic: For major policies and major reforms, the court gathers the deliberations of its ministers at home, and abroad it sometimes awaits memorials from frontier officials.

sentences.zh: 勤求民隱，博采公論，與立憲之制無不符合。

translations.literal: Diligently seeking the people's hidden grievances, broadly gathering public opinion—this in no way fails to accord with constitutional systems.
translations.idiomatic: In diligently seeking the people's hidden grievances and broadly gathering public opinion, our practices are fully in accord with constitutional systems.

sentences.zh: 上有教誡無約誓，下有遵守無要求。

translations.literal: Above there is instruction and admonition without covenant and oath; below there is compliance without demanding requirements.
translations.idiomatic: Above, there is instruction and admonition without binding covenants; below, there is obedience without pressing demands.

sentences.zh: 至日久官吏失職，或有奉行之不善，海國開通，又有事例之所無，自可因時損益，並非變法更張。

translations.literal: As for over time officials and functionaries derelict in duty, or something badly carried out in implementation—with maritime countries opened there are also matters without precedent—one may naturally increase or decrease according to the times; this is not changing the law and overturning institutions.
translations.idiomatic: When over time officials neglect their duties or something is poorly carried out, or when the opening of maritime trade brings matters without precedent, one may naturally adjust according to the times; this is not a fundamental change of law and institutions.

sentences.zh: 惟人心趣向各異，告以堯、舜、周、孔之道，則以爲不足法；

translations.literal: Only people's minds' orientations each differ: tell them the Ways of Yao, Shun, the Zhou, and Confucius—they then consider them insufficient as models;
translations.idiomatic: Only people's inclinations differ: tell them the ways of Yao, Shun, the Zhou, and Confucius, and they deem them unworthy of imitation;

sentences.zh: 告以英、德、法、美之制度，而日本所模仿者，則心悅誠服，以爲當行。

translations.literal: tell them the systems of Britain, Germany, France, and America—and what Japan imitated—they are pleased in heart and sincere in submission, considering them what ought to be enacted.
translations.idiomatic: tell them the systems of Britain, Germany, France, and America—and what Japan has imitated—and they are wholeheartedly convinced that these should be adopted at once.

sentences.zh: 考日本維新之初，即宣言立憲之意。

translations.literal: Examining Japan at the beginning of the Restoration, it at once proclaimed the intent of constitutionalism.
translations.idiomatic: If we examine Japan at the beginning of the Meiji Restoration, it at once proclaimed its intention to adopt constitutional government.

sentences.zh: 後十四年，始發布開設國會之敕諭，二十年乃頒行憲法。

translations.literal: Fourteen years later it first issued the imperial rescript opening a national assembly; only after twenty years did it promulgate the constitution.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen years later it first issued the imperial rescript convening a national assembly, and only after twenty years did it promulgate a constitution.

sentences.zh: 蓋預備詳密遲慎如此。

translations.literal: Thus its preparation was detailed, slow, and cautious to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Its preparation was thus so detailed, slow, and cautious.

sentences.zh: 今橫議者自謂國民，聚衆者輒云團體，數年之中，內治外交，用人行政，皆有干預之想。

translations.literal: Now those who rashly debate call themselves nationals; those who gather in crowds often say groups—in a few years' span, in internal governance and foreign relations, in employment of personnel and administration, all have thoughts of intervening.
translations.idiomatic: Today those who speak rashly in public call themselves "the people," and those who assemble in crowds call themselves "organizations"; within a few years they have come to think they may intervene in domestic governance, foreign relations, appointments, and administration alike.

sentences.zh: 動以立憲爲詞，紛馳電函，上厪宸慮。

translations.literal: They move, taking constitutionalism as their phrase; they rush about like lightning dispatches, vexing the Imperial Mind's deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: They constantly invoke constitutionalism, sending urgent telegrams that trouble the emperor's peace of mind.

sentences.zh: 蓋以立憲爲新奇可喜，不知吾國所自有。

translations.literal: They take constitutionalism as novel and pleasing, not knowing what our country already possesses on its own.
translations.idiomatic: They treat constitutionalism as something novel and delightful, unaware that our country already possesses it in its own way.

sentences.zh: 其關於學術者，固貽譏荒陋，以立憲爲即可施行，不審東洋之近事。

translations.literal: As for what concerns learning and doctrine, they indeed invite ridicule as crude and shallow—thinking constitutionalism can at once be implemented, not examining recent affairs in the Eastern Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: In matters of learning they invite ridicule for their shallowness, imagining that constitutionalism can be put into effect immediately without studying recent events in the Eastern seas.

sentences.zh: 關於政術者，尤有害治安。

translations.literal: As for what concerns political methods, it is especially harmful to peace and order.
translations.idiomatic: In matters of political method they are especially harmful to public order.

sentences.zh: 惟在朝廷本一定之指歸，齊萬衆之心志，循序漸進。

translations.literal: Only the court must hold to one fixed orientation and align the myriad hearts' aspirations, advancing step by step in due sequence.
translations.idiomatic: What is needed is for the court to hold to a single clear direction, align the minds of the multitude, and advance step by step.

sentences.zh: 先設京師議院以定從違，舉辦地方自治以植根本，尤要在廣興教育，儲備人才。

translations.literal: First establish an assembly at the capital to fix assent and dissent; widely undertake local self-government to plant foundations; especially important is broadly promoting education and storing up talented persons.
translations.idiomatic: First establish a deliberative assembly at the capital to determine what is to be accepted or rejected; promote local self-government to lay foundations; and above all expand education and train talent.

sentences.zh: 凡與憲政相輔而行者，均當先事綢繆者也。

translations.literal: Whatever assists and proceeds together with constitutional government ought all to be planned beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Everything that must accompany constitutional government should be prepared in advance.

sentences.zh: 臣前隨李鴻章至柏林，略觀大概。

translations.literal: Your servant formerly followed Li Hongzhang to Berlin and briefly observed the general situation.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant once followed Li Hongzhang to Berlin and gained some general acquaintance with the system there.

sentences.zh: 今承特簡，謹當參合中、西同異，歸極於皇朝典章，庶言皆有本而事屬可行。

translations.literal: Now receiving special selection, I shall carefully combine Chinese and Western similarities and differences and converge upon the imperial court's statutes and regulations—hoping that words all have foundation and affairs belong to what can be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Now, entrusted with this special mission, I shall carefully compare Chinese and Western similarities and differences and bring them into harmony with the statutes of the imperial court, so that every proposal has a solid basis and every measure can be carried out.

sentences.zh: 是臣區區之至願。」

translations.literal: This is your servant's humble utmost wish."
translations.idiomatic: This is your servant's humble and earnest wish."

sentences.zh: 明年，調禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: The next year transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 時新黨要求實行立憲，召集國會日亟。

translations.literal: At that time the new faction urgently demanded implementing constitutionalism and summoning the national assembly day by day.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the reform party urgently demanded that constitutional government be implemented and a national assembly convened without delay.

sentences.zh: 式枚上言：「臣徧考東西歷史，參校同異，大抵中法皆定自上而下奉行，西法則定自下而上遵守。

translations.literal: Shimei submitted saying: "Your servant has broadly examined Eastern and Western history and compared similarities and differences; broadly speaking, Chinese methods are all fixed from above and implemented downward; Western methods are fixed from below and obeyed upward.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei memorialized, saying: "Your servant has broadly examined the histories of East and West and compared their differences; in general, Chinese methods are established from above and carried out downward, whereas Western methods are established from below and obeyed upward.

sentences.zh: 惟日本憲法，則纂自日臣伊藤博文，雖西國之名詞，仍東洋之性質。

translations.literal: Only Japan's constitution was compiled by the Japanese minister Ito Hirobumi—though Western country terminology, it still has an Eastern Ocean nature.
translations.idiomatic: Only Japan's constitution was drafted by the Japanese minister Ito Hirobumi; though it employs Western terminology, it retains an East Asian character.

sentences.zh: 其采取則普魯士爲多，其本原則德君臣所定，名爲欽定憲法。

translations.literal: What it adopted was mostly Prussia; its origin was fixed by sovereign and ministers of Germany; it is called an emperor-given constitution.
translations.idiomatic: In what it adopted Prussia predominated; its foundation was laid by the sovereign and ministers of Germany, and it is called an emperor-granted constitution.

sentences.zh: 夫國所以立曰政，政所以行曰權，權所歸即利所在。

translations.literal: The state is therefore established—this is called government; government is therefore carried out—this is called power; wherever power returns is where benefit lies.
translations.idiomatic: A state is established for the sake of government, government is exercised through power, and wherever power resides, there interest lies as well.

sentences.zh: 定於一則無非分之想，散於衆則有競進之心。

translations.literal: Fixed in one place then there are no improper thoughts; dispersed among the multitude then there are competitive advancing hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When power is fixed in one place, improper ambitions do not arise; when it is dispersed among the multitude, hearts compete to advance.

sentences.zh: 行之而善，則爲日本之維新；

translations.literal: If carried out well, then it is like Japan's Restoration;
translations.idiomatic: If it is carried out well, the result is Japan's Meiji Restoration;

sentences.zh: 行之不善，則爲法國之革命。

translations.literal: if carried out poorly, then it is like France's revolution.
translations.idiomatic: if it is carried out poorly, the result is France's revolution.

sentences.zh: 法國當屢世苛虐之後，民困已深，欲以立憲救亡，而適促其亂。

translations.literal: France at the time after generations of harsh cruelty, the people were deeply distressed; wishing to use constitutionalism to save extinction, it happened to hasten its disorder.
translations.idiomatic: France, after generations of harsh rule, was a country whose people were already deeply afflicted; hoping to save itself through constitutional government, it only hastened its disorder.

sentences.zh: 日本當尊王傾幕之時，本由民力，故以立憲爲報，而猶緩其期。

translations.literal: Japan at the time of revering the emperor and overthrowing the shogunate, originally relied on popular strength; therefore it took constitutionalism as repayment—yet still slowed its timetable.
translations.idiomatic: Japan, at the time of the movement to honor the emperor and overthrow the shogunate, had relied on popular strength; it therefore offered constitutional government in return, yet still moved slowly.

sentences.zh: 中國名義最重，政治最寬，國體尊嚴，人情安習，既無法國之怨毒，又非日本之改造。

translations.literal: China's nominal propriety is weightiest, governance most lenient, state body most dignified, human sentiment most accustomed to peace—having neither France's bitter poisons nor Japan's reconstruction.
translations.idiomatic: China places the greatest weight on ritual propriety, governs with the greatest leniency, possesses the most dignified state form, and its people are most accustomed to settled life; it has neither France's accumulated bitterness nor Japan's need for wholesale reconstruction.

sentences.zh: 皇上俯順輿情，迭降諭旨，分定年期，自宜互相奮勉，靜待推行。

translations.literal: The Emperor, deferring to popular sentiment, repeatedly issued edicts setting term years—naturally all should mutually exert themselves and calmly await implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, deferring to public sentiment, has repeatedly issued edicts setting a timetable; all should therefore encourage one another and calmly await implementation.

sentences.zh: 豈容欲速等於取償，求治同於論價？

translations.literal: How can one tolerate desiring speed equal to taking repayment, seeking order the same as bargaining a price?
translations.idiomatic: How can we tolerate demanding speed as though collecting a debt, or treating good government like haggling over a price?

sentences.zh: 至敢言監督朝廷，推倒政府，胥動浮言，幾同亂黨。

translations.literal: As for those who dare speak of supervising the court and overthrowing the government—all move empty words, nearly the same as disruptive factions.
translations.idiomatic: As for those who dare speak of supervising the court or overthrowing the government, they traffic in reckless talk and are nearly indistinguishable from seditious factions.

sentences.zh: 欲圖補救之策，惟在朝廷舉錯一秉至公，不稍予以指摘之端，自無從爲煽惑之計。

translations.literal: The policy to seek remedy lies only in the court's every action and pause holding to utmost fairness, not slightly giving grounds for criticism—then naturally there is no means for schemes of incitement.
translations.idiomatic: The remedy lies solely in the court holding every action to the utmost standard of fairness and giving no handle for criticism; then there will naturally be no opportunity for agitation.

sentences.zh: 至東南各省疆吏，當慎擇有風力、知大體者鎮懾之。

translations.literal: As for southeastern provinces' frontier officials, one should carefully choose those with force of character who understand the larger pattern to control and restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: As for the frontier officials of the southeastern provinces, men of forceful character who understand the larger situation should be carefully chosen to keep order.

sentences.zh: 當十年預備之期，爲大局安危所繫。

translations.literal: During the ten-year preparatory period, the larger situation's safety and danger are bound up.
translations.idiomatic: During the ten-year preparatory period, the safety of the whole situation is at stake.

sentences.zh: 日皇所謂『組織權限，爲朕親裁』，德相所謂『法定於君，非民可解』。

translations.literal: What the Japanese emperor called "organize authority, personally adjudicated by Us"; what the German chancellor called "law fixed by the sovereign, not for the people to interpret."
translations.idiomatic: As the Japanese emperor said, "the organization of authority is personally determined by Us"; as the German chancellor said, "the law is fixed by the sovereign and is not for the people to interpret."

sentences.zh: 故必正名定分，然後措正施行。

translations.literal: Therefore one must correct names and fix allotments—only then can rectification and implementation be set.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore names and roles must first be properly defined; only then can measures be rightly applied.

sentences.zh: 臣濫膺考察，斷不敢附會時趨，貽誤國家，得罪名教。」

translations.literal: Your servant undeservedly received the commission of investigation; I absolutely dare not attach to current fashion, erring against the state and offending against the teaching of names."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has undeservedly received this commission of investigation; I dare not simply follow the fashion of the day, to the harm of the state and the offense of right principle."

sentences.zh: 章下所司。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 尋調吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was transferred to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 上海政聞社法部主事陳景仁等電請定三年內開國會，罷式枚謝天下，嚴旨申飭，褫景仁職。

translations.literal: Chen Jingren of the Ministry of Justice bureau and others of the Political Opinion Society in Shanghai telegraphed requesting a national assembly within three years and that Shimei be dismissed to appease the realm; a stern edict reprimanded; Jingren's office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingren, a bureau secretary in the Ministry of Justice, and others of the Political Opinion Society in Shanghai telegraphed demanding that a national assembly be convened within three years and that Shimei be dismissed to appease public opinion; a stern edict rebuked them and stripped Chen Jingren of his post.

sentences.zh: 式枚復奏言：「德皇接受國書，答言憲政紛繁，慮未必合中國用，選舉法尤未易行。

translations.literal: Shimei again memorialized, saying: "When the German emperor received the credentials, he replied that constitutional affairs are numerous and complex—worried they might not suit China's use; election law especially is not easy to implement.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei memorialized again, saying: "When the German emperor received the credentials of investiture, he replied that constitutional affairs are complex and numerous and might not suit China's needs; election law in particular would be difficult to implement.

sentences.zh: 又昔英儒斯賓塞爾亦甚言憲法流弊，謂美國憲法本人民平等，行之久而治權握於政黨，平民不勝其苦。

translations.literal: Moreover, formerly the English scholar Spencer also spoke greatly of constitutionalism's abuses, saying America's constitution originally held popular equality—in long implementation governing power was grasped by political parties and common people could not bear the suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the English scholar Herbert Spencer also spoke at length of the abuses of constitutional government, saying that although the American constitution was founded on popular equality, in the long run governing power fell into the hands of political parties and the common people could not bear the suffering.

sentences.zh: 蓋歐人言憲法，其難其慎如此。

translations.literal: Thus when Europeans speak of constitutions, the difficulty and caution are like this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when Europeans speak of constitutions, their difficulty and caution are of this order.

sentences.zh: 今橫議遍於國中，上則詆政府固權，下則罵國民失職，專以爭競相勸導。

translations.literal: Now rash debate fills the country: above they slander the government's solidifying power; below they revile nationals for dereliction of duty—dedicated to taking competition as encouragement and guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Today reckless debate fills the country: above, the government is accused of monopolizing power; below, the people are blamed for failing in their duties—all while competition alone is preached as the path forward.

sentences.zh: 此正斯賓塞爾所云政黨者流，與平民固無與也。

translations.literal: This is exactly what Spencer called the stream of political parties—it fundamentally has nothing to do with common people.
translations.idiomatic: This is precisely what Spencer called the party faction—it has nothing to do with the common people.

sentences.zh: 伊藤博文論君臣相與，先道德而後科條。

translations.literal: Ito Hirobumi discussed sovereign and minister interacting: first morality, afterward statutes and items.
translations.idiomatic: Ito Hirobumi observed that in the relation between sovereign and minister, morality comes first and statutes afterward.

sentences.zh: 君民何獨不然？

translations.literal: Is the relation between ruler and people alone not so?
translations.idiomatic: Is the relation between ruler and people any different?

sentences.zh: 果能誠信相接，則普與日本以欽定憲法行之至今；

translations.literal: If truly able to connect in sincerity and trust, then broadly with Japan using the emperor-given constitution practiced to this day;
translations.idiomatic: If sincerity and trust can truly be maintained, then constitutional government may broadly be practiced as in Japan, which has used an emperor-granted constitution down to the present;

sentences.zh: 如其不然，則法蘭西固民約憲法，何以革命者再三，改法者數十而猶未定？

translations.literal: if not so, then France indeed has a people's covenant constitution—why have revolutions again and again, why have changes of law dozens of times yet still not settled?
translations.idiomatic: if not, then consider France, which indeed has a constitution based on a covenant of the people—why has it suffered repeated revolutions and dozens of changes of law without ever settling?

sentences.zh: 臣愚以爲中國立憲，應以日本仿照普魯士之例爲權衡，以畢士麥由君主用人民意見制定，及伊藤博文先道德後科條之言爲標準，則憲法大綱立矣。」

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly considers that China's establishing constitutionalism should take Japan's imitating Prussia as the balance; take Bismarck's formulation by the sovereign using the people's opinions, and Ito Hirobumi's words of morality before statutes, as standards—then the constitution's grand outline is established."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant humbly believes that in establishing constitutional government China should take Japan's imitation of Prussia as its measure, and Bismarck's principle that the sovereign should formulate law with reference to the people's views, together with Ito Hirobumi's teaching that morality must precede statutes, as its standards; then the grand outline of a constitution may be laid down."

sentences.zh: 章下所司。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 又以各省諮議局章程與普國地方議會制度不符，大恉謂：「改革未定之時，中央政權唯恐少統一堅强之力，而國民識政體知法意者極少。

translations.literal: He also, because each province's consultative assembly regulations did not accord with Prussian local assembly institutions, greatly angrily said: "At a time when reform is not yet settled, central authority only fears having too little unified solid strength—while nationals who understand the political body and know the meaning of law are extremely few.
translations.idiomatic: He also protested vigorously that the regulations for provincial consultative assemblies did not accord with Prussian local assemblies, declaring: "At a time when reform is still unsettled, central authority can scarcely afford to lose unified strength, while those among the people who understand the political order and the meaning of law are extremely few.

sentences.zh: 驟以此龐大政權之地方議會，橫亙政府與國民之間，縱使被選者不皆營私武斷，而一國政權落於最少數人之手，劫持中外大臣，後患何可勝言？」

translations.literal: Suddenly to place this enormous authority of local assemblies horizontally between government and nationals—even if those elected are not all seeking private gain and arbitrarily judging—still one country's political power falls into the hands of the very few, hijacking Chinese and foreign ministers; later troubles—how can words exhaust them?"
translations.idiomatic: To thrust suddenly between government and people a local assembly wielding such vast authority—even if those elected were not all selfish and domineering—would still place the political power of the entire country in the hands of a tiny minority, able to hold ministers Chinese and foreign hostage; the later troubles are beyond words."

sentences.zh: 因證以普制，逐條駁議。

translations.literal: Thus proving by Prussian institutions, he refuted item by item.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore cited Prussian institutions and refuted the proposals article by article.

sentences.zh: 先後譯奏普魯士憲法全文、官制位號等級，暨兩議院新舊選舉法。

translations.literal: Before and after he translated and memorialized the full text of the Prussian constitution, official ranks and grades, and both assemblies' new and old election laws.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after he translated and presented memorials containing the full text of the Prussian constitution, the ranks and grades of officialdom, and the new and old election laws of both chambers.

sentences.zh: 式枚以三十三年冬行，宣統元年六月返國，以疾乞假。

translations.literal: Shimei departed in the winter of the thirty-third year; in the sixth month of the first Xuantong year returned to the country; citing illness he begged leave.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei set out in the winter of the thirty-third year and returned home in the sixth month of the first Xuantong year, then begged leave on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 張之洞遺疏薦式枚堪大用。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhidong's final memorial recommended Shimei as fit for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: In his deathbed memorial Zhang Zhidong recommended Yu Shimei as capable of great service.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部侍郎，改學部侍郎，總理禮學館事、修訂法律大臣、國史館副總裁。

translations.literal: Transferred Vice Minister of Personnel, changed to Vice Minister of Education, directed affairs of the Hall of Ritual Learning, Revising Laws Minister, and Deputy President of the National History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of personnel, then reassigned as vice minister of education, and also directed the Hall of Ritual Learning, served as revising laws minister, and was deputy president of the National History Institute.

sentences.zh: 國變後，僑居青島。

translations.literal: After the change of dynasty he lived in exile in Qingdao.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the dynasty he lived in retirement in Qingdao.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，年六十三，諡文和。

translations.literal: Before long he died, age sixty-three; posthumous title Wenhe.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died at the age of sixty-three and was given the posthumous title Wenhe.

sentences.zh: 式枚生而隱宮，精力絕人，夜倚枕坐如枯僧。

translations.literal: Shimei from birth had hidden palace; his energy was surpassing men; at night he leaned on a pillow sitting like a withered monk.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei was born with cryptorchidism, yet his vitality was extraordinary; at night he would sit propped on a pillow like a withered monk.

sentences.zh: 內介而外和易。

translations.literal: Inside stern, outside mild and easy.
translations.idiomatic: Inwardly he was severe, outwardly mild and approachable.

sentences.zh: 論事謇諤，頗有聲公卿間云。

translations.literal: In discussing affairs blunt and upright—he had quite a reputation among dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In debate he was blunt and forthright, and he enjoyed considerable reputation among the high officials.

sentences.zh: 沈家本，字子惇，浙江歸安人。

translations.literal: Shen Jiaben, zi Zidun, a man of Gui'an, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jiaben, whose courtesy name was Zidun, was a native of Gui'an in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 少讀書，好深湛之思，於周官多創獲。

translations.literal: In youth he read books and loved deep, profound thought; in the Rites of Zhou he made many original discoveries.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he read widely and loved deep reflection; in the Rites of Zhou he made many original discoveries.

sentences.zh: 初援例以郎中分刑部，博稽掌故，多所纂述。

translations.literal: At first by purchased degree he entered as a Department Director split to the Ministry of Punishments; broadly examined established practice and made many compilations.
translations.idiomatic: At first, by purchased degree, he entered service as a department director assigned to the Ministry of Punishments, where he broadly investigated precedent and compiled many works.

sentences.zh: 光緒九年，成進士，仍留部。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Guangxu he completed jinshi and remained at the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Guangxu reign he passed the metropolitan examination and remained at the ministry.

sentences.zh: 補官後，充主稿，兼秋審處。

translations.literal: After receiving substantive appointment he served as chief drafter and concurrently in the Autumn Review Office.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving a substantive appointment he served as chief drafter and concurrently in the Autumn Review Office.

sentences.zh: 自此遂專心法律之學，爲尚書潘祖蔭所稱賞。

translations.literal: From this he devoted himself to the study of law and was praised and appreciated by Minister Pan Zuyin.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he devoted himself to legal studies and won the praise of Minister Pan Zuyin.

sentences.zh: 十九年，出知天津府，治尚寬大，姦民易之，聚衆鬨於市，即擒斬四人，無敢復犯者。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he went out as prefect of Tianjin. His governance favored leniency; ruffians took him lightly and gathered a mob to make trouble in the market. He immediately seized and executed four men, and none dared offend again.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was appointed prefect of Tianjin. His rule favored leniency, and local ruffians took him lightly until a mob rioted in the market. He had four ringleaders seized and executed at once, and no one dared repeat the offense.

sentences.zh: 調劇保定，甘軍毀法國教堂，當路懾於外勢，償五萬金，以道署舊址建新堂，侵及府署東偏。

translations.literal: He was transferred to turbulent Baoding. Gansu troops destroyed a French church. Those in power were afraid of foreign pressure and paid fifty thousand taels, building a new church on the old site of the circuit intendant's yamen, encroaching on the east side of the prefectural yamen.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to troubled Baoding, where Gansu troops destroyed a French church. The authorities, fearing foreign pressure, paid fifty thousand taels and built a new church on the old circuit yamen site, encroaching on the east wing of the prefectural offices.

sentences.zh: 家本據府志力爭得直。

translations.literal: Jiaben argued forcefully on the basis of the prefectural gazetteer and won his case.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaben argued forcefully from the prefectural gazetteer and won his case.

sentences.zh: 拳匪亂作，家本已擢通永道、山西按察使，未及行，兩宮西幸。

translations.literal: When the Boxer uprising broke out, Jiaben had already been promoted to circuit intendant of Tongzhou and Yongping and surveillance commissioner of Shanxi, but before he could take up his posts the two palaces went west.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer uprising broke out, Jiaben had already been promoted to circuit intendant of Tongzhou and Yongping and to surveillance commissioner of Shanxi, but before he could take up his posts the court fled west.

sentences.zh: 聯軍入保定，教士銜前隙，誣以助拳匪，卒無左驗而解。

translations.literal: When the allied armies entered Baoding, missionaries nursed old grudges and accused him of aiding the Boxers, but in the end no corroborating evidence was found and the case was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies entered Baoding, missionaries nursed old grievances and accused him of aiding the Boxers, but in the end no evidence supported the charge and the case was dropped.

sentences.zh: 因馳赴行在，授光祿寺卿，擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He therefore hurried to the traveling court and was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He hurried to the traveling court, where he was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and then promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 自各國互市以來，內地許傳教，而中外用律輕重懸殊，民、教日齟齬。
