translations.literal: Since the various countries began mutual trade, missionary work was permitted in the interior, but Chinese and foreign law differed greatly in severity, and friction between people and missionaries grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Since the treaty ports opened, missionaries were allowed in the interior, but Chinese and foreign law differed sharply in severity, and friction between common people and missionaries grew daily.

sentences.zh: 官畏事則務抑民，民不能堪，則激而一逞，往往焚戮成巨禍。

translations.literal: Officials, fearing trouble, would suppress the people; when the people could not endure it they would erupt in violence, and often burning and killing became great catastrophes.
translations.idiomatic: Officials, fearing trouble, would suppress the people; when the people could no longer bear it they would erupt in violence, and burning and killing often became catastrophes.

sentences.zh: 家本以謂治今日之民，當令官吏普通法律。

translations.literal: Jiaben held that to govern the people of today one must make officials generally understand law.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaben held that to govern the people of today, officials must be made generally conversant with the law.

sentences.zh: 然中律不變而欲收回領事審判權，終不可得。

translations.literal: Yet if the Chinese code remained unchanged while one wished to recover consular jurisdiction, it could never be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if the Chinese code remained unchanged, recovering consular jurisdiction would remain impossible.

sentences.zh: 會變法議起，袁世凱奏設修訂法律館，命家本偕伍廷芳總其事；

translations.literal: When discussion of reform arose, Yuan Shikai memorialized establishing the Commission for the Revision of Laws, ordering Jiaben together with Wu Tingfang to take general charge of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When reform was debated, Yuan Shikai memorialized to establish the Commission for the Revision of Laws and ordered Jiaben and Wu Tingfang to direct it jointly.

sentences.zh: 別設法律學堂，畢業者近千人，一時稱盛。

translations.literal: A separate law school was established, with nearly a thousand graduates; for a time it was greatly celebrated.
translations.idiomatic: A separate law school was established, with nearly a thousand graduates, and for a time it was widely acclaimed.

sentences.zh: 補大理寺卿，旋改法部侍郎，充修訂法律大臣。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Court of Judicial Review, soon changed to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Law, and served as commissioner for the revision of laws.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of the Court of Judicial Review, soon became vice minister of the Ministry of Law, and served as commissioner for the revision of laws.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，兼資政院副總裁，仍日與館員商訂諸法草案，先後告成，未嘗以事繁自解。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong he concurrently served as Vice President of the Political Consultative Assembly, yet still daily discussed draft laws with the bureau members; they were completed in succession, and he never excused himself because of pressing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuantong he also served as vice president of the Political Consultative Assembly, yet still met daily with bureau staff to draft laws. The codes were completed one after another, and he never pleaded the press of business as an excuse to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 其所著書，有讀律校勘記、秋讞須知、刑案匯覽、刺字集、律例偶箋、歷代刑官考、歷代刑法考、漢律摭遺、明大誥竣令考、明律目箋，他所著非刑律者又二十餘種，都二百餘卷。

translations.literal: His writings included Collation Notes on Reading the Code, Essentials for Autumn Review Cases, Compendium of Criminal Cases, Collection on Tattooing, Occasional Commentary on Statutes and Regulations, Study of Punishment Officials through the Ages, Study of Punishment Law through the Ages, Gathered Remains of Han Law, Study of the Ming Great Admonitions and Completed Commands, and Commentary on the Ming Code Table of Contents; his non-penal writings numbered more than twenty additional works, totaling more than two hundred juan.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included Collation Notes on Reading the Code, Essentials for Autumn Review Cases, Compendium of Criminal Cases, Collection on Tattooing, Occasional Commentary on Statutes and Regulations, Study of Punishment Officials through the Ages, Study of Punishment Law through the Ages, Gathered Remains of Han Law, Study of the Ming Great Admonitions and Completed Commands, and Commentary on the Ming Code Table of Contents, along with more than twenty other works not on penal law, totaling over two hundred juan.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自變法議興，凡新政特設大臣領之。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Since discussion of reform arose, every new policy was specially entrusted to a grand minister to lead.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Once reform was debated, every new policy was placed under a specially appointed grand minister.

sentences.zh: 百熙管學務，家本修法律，並邀時譽。

translations.literal: Baixi directed educational affairs and Jiaben revised the laws; both won contemporary praise.
translations.idiomatic: Baixi directed educational affairs and Jiaben revised the laws; both won contemporary acclaim.

sentences.zh: 景崇之主教育，謀溝通新舊；

translations.literal: Jingchong directed education and sought to bridge old and new.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong directed education and sought to reconcile the old and the new.

sentences.zh: 式枚之論憲政，務因時損益。

translations.literal: Shimei discussed constitutional government and sought timely adjustment and benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei discussed constitutional government and sought timely adjustment rather than rigid change.

sentences.zh: 而大勢所趨，已莫能挽救。

translations.literal: But the trend of the great situation already could not be reversed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the tide of events could no longer be turned back.

sentences.zh: 家鼐儒厚廉謹，常以資望領新政，每參大計，獨持正不阿。

translations.literal: Jianai was learned, generous, honest and cautious; he often led new policies by senior standing, took part in every great plan, and alone held to principle without trimming his views to please.
translations.idiomatic: Jianai was learned, generous, honest, and cautious. He often headed new policies by virtue of senior standing, took part in every major decision, and alone upheld principle without trimming his views to please.

sentences.zh: 賢哉，不愧古大臣矣！

translations.literal: How worthy! He did not disgrace the great ministers of antiquity!
translations.idiomatic: How worthy a man—he did not disgrace the great ministers of old!
